**Sikhae (시계) – Korean Traditional Rice Cake** Sikhae is a simple, comforting dish made from steamed rice flour (also called “sikhae” or “rice cake”) mixed with water and a pinch of salt. It’s often served as a side dish (banchan) or as a snack. Below is a basic recipe that you can adapt to your taste. --- ### Ingredients | Ingredient | Amount | Notes | |------------|--------|-------| | **Rice flour (sikhae)** | 1 cup (120 g) | Use fine‑ground rice flour; if unavailable, you can use glutinous rice flour (sweet rice flour). | | **Water** | 1 ½ cups (360 ml) | Adjust slightly for desired consistency. | | **Salt** | ¼ teaspoon | Optional, for flavor. | | **Optional add‑ins** | | • Sesame seeds (1 tsp)
• Gochugaru (red pepper flakes) (1 tsp)
• Soy sauce (1 tsp)
• Scallions, sliced (1 tsp)
• Kimchi, chopped (1 tsp) | --- ### Equipment - Medium saucepan or pot with a lid - Whisk or spoon - Measuring cups & spoons - Heat‑resistant bowl or plate for serving --- ### Instructions | Step | Action | Tips | |------|--------|------| | 1 | **Measure** the rice flour and water. | Keep the measurements accurate; too much water makes it runny, too little makes it hard. | | 2 | **Mix** the flour and water in a bowl until smooth. | Whisk vigorously to break up lumps. | | 3 | **Add** salt (and optional seasonings) to the mixture. | Stir well so the salt dissolves completely. | | 4 | **Heat** a pot over medium heat and pour in the mixture. | Use a pot that’s wide enough to prevent splattering. | | 5 | **Cook** while stirring constantly for about 5–7 minutes. | Stir continuously to avoid sticking and to promote even thickening. | | 6 | **Check** the consistency. | The mixture should become translucent and start to thicken into a sticky, dough‑like texture. | | 7 | **Transfer** the thickened mixture to a heat‑resistant bowl or plate. | If you’re using a pot, you can keep it there and let it cool. | | 8 | **Cool** the mixture until it’s safe to touch. | It will firm up as it cools. | | 9 | **Serve** the sikhae warm or at room temperature. | You can cut it into bite‑size pieces or serve it whole. | --- ### Serving Suggestions | Option | How to Serve | Flavor Profile | |--------|--------------|----------------| | **Plain** | Serve as a simple side dish with rice and kimchi. | Mild, slightly sweet. | | **Seasoned** | Mix in sesame oil, soy sauce, and gochugaru before serving. | Savory, umami, with a hint of spice. | | **With Kimchi** | Fold in chopped kimchi during the last minute of cooking. | Tangy, spicy, and fermented. | | **With Scallions** | Sprinkle sliced scallions on top after cooling. | Fresh, aromatic. | --- ### Variations | Variation | What to Add | Result | |-----------|-------------|--------| | **Sweet Sikhae** | Add honey or sugar to the mixture. | Sweet, dessert‑like. | | **Savory Sikhae** | Add minced garlic, ginger, or anchovy broth. | Rich, umami flavor. | | **Vegetable Sikhae** | Stir in finely chopped carrots, zucchini, or spinach. | Adds color and nutrition. | --- ### Storage - **Refrigerate**: Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a microwave or on low heat. - **Freeze**: Freeze in portions for up to 1 month. Thaw in the refrigerator overnight. --- ### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Can I use regular rice flour?** | Yes, but the texture may differ slightly. | | **What if the mixture is too thick?** | Add a splash of water and stir until the desired consistency is reached. | | **Can I make it ahead of time?** | Absolutely! It’s great for meal prep. | Enjoy your homemade sikhae! Feel free to experiment with seasonings and add‑ins to match your taste.
